If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overshoot.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is trending downward, reverse the adjustment: increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon to align with sentiment momentum.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 1.0–2.0% for mid horizon to correct for sentiment-driven overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is flat, apply no adjustment for late horizon unless true outcome shows divergence >1.5% from forecast — then reduce by 0.5–1.0% to avoid inertia bias.
